Definition: the earth (as moist and therefore inhabited); by extension, the globe; by implication, its inhabitants; specifically, a particular land, as Babylonia, Palestine
BiblicalUsage: The word is the world, the inhabited earth, the whole round of it. The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof, the world, and they that dwell therein; before the mountains were brought forth, or ever Thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, Thou art God. Isaiah says the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness when God's judgments are in the earth, and Hannah sings that the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and He hath set the world upon them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the world is the Lord's from the beginning, not ours to own, and He formed it before the mountains stood. My position is that the world and all who live in it answer to Him, and His judgments teach its inhabitants righteousness.
